Subject: Dedicated capacity request — H200 family + short-term burst

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran an internal planning session and have a tight procurement window — we need to lock dedicated capacity for an upcoming clinical imaging trial starting Aug 2. Key asks: 
- Reserved capacity: 6x H200 (32GB variant) or equivalent — workload requires the H200 family for sustained fp8 inference.
- Burst: ability to burst an extra 12 GPUs for up to 8 weeks during the trial window.
- Reservation hold: can you hold the reservation for two weeks while our procurement completes the PO?
- Pricing: SolaceMed is asking for a 25% discount off list on the reservation (we will commit 24 months).

Attached: solacemed_capacity_request.xlsx (forecast + trial schedule). Procurement is asking for a written confirmation of terms by 2027-07-22 to hit our supplier cutoff.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate H200 reservation holds and a capped burst surcharge?

— Marie
Head of Infrastructure, SolaceMed

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15T16:40:00Z
Subject: RE: SolaceMed H200 request — proposed concession package for exec review

Team,

Summary of recommended concession package to present to Execs:
- Reservation: 6x H200-32GB, 24-month commitment. List reservation price = $X/month (confidential in email).
- Reservation discount: 25% off list (customer requests).
- Burst: allow +12 GPUs for up to 8 weeks in trial window. Standard burst surcharge is 50% of on-demand reservation rate; propose capping burst surcharge at 30% for this window (to keep predictability).
- Reservation hold: hold allocation for 14 days (to allow PO routing).
- Conditions: signed addendum that the trial usage is only for the specified dates, and that any additional sustained usage beyond the 8-week window will be charged at standard overage. Legal to prepare addendum.

Rationale: 24-month commit + documented clinical trial reduces churn risk. H200 is a material ops change and increases exposure; we’re effectively provisioning scarce H200 capacity ahead of release, so the hold and discount together are a meaningful concession.

Ask: Exec sign-off required for reservation discount >=20% and for H200 family reservation holds. If we get approval today we can provide Marie a formal addendum + DocuSign before the 7/22 cutoff.

Attachments: none (Vanessa has the draft terms).

Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15T17:10:00Z
Subject: RE: SolaceMed H200 request — finance/legal pre-check

Agree with the summary. A few finance/legal points before we escalate to Exec: 
- Margin impact: 25% discount + capped burst materially reduces first-year margin; need to confirm whether we can split discounts (e.g., 22% for year 1, 10% for year 2) to protect longer-term economics.
- Operational exposure: H200 reservation hold increases capacity risk; ops needs to confirm availability window. Ops (Rishi) please confirm we can reserve H200 family capacity and that holding will not block higher-priority requests if capacity runs tight.
- Legal: addendum must include strict trial dates and overage terms; no retroactive changes.

If Ops confirms capacity and we can structure a staged discount (22% year1 / 10% year2), I recommend we present that to Exec as the ask. That may increase sign-off probability.

I’ll prep a one-pager for Marissa with the proposed numbers and ask. Vanessa, can you add a short justification paragraph from SolaceMed (clinical trial importance + PR/strategic value)? I will attach the exec approval form.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-07-15T18:02:00Z
Subject: RE: SolaceMed H200 request — EXEC DECISION

Thanks team for the quick turnaround. I reviewed the one-pager Lauren is preparing. Decision (conditional):
- Approve a concession for SolaceMed, with the following limits:
  - Reservation discount: 22% for year 1, 10% for year 2 (instead of requested 25% flat).
  - Burst surcharge cap: 35% for the 8-week window (compromise to balance customer ask vs. ops exposure).
  - Reservation hold: approve a 6-week hold (not 14 days) — this minimizes capacity blocking.

Conditions before legal/ops finalize:
- Legal must draft an addendum (DocuSign) with explicit trial dates, overage triggers, and clawback if trial extends beyond agreed window.
- Finance to accept the 22%/10% staged discount as final for quoting.
- Ops (Rishi) to confirm absolute availability of 6x H200 + ability to support 12 GPU bursts during the trial; if not possible, we revert to an H100-equivalent with adjusted pricing.

Vanessa — please respond to SolaceMed that we have conditional approval and indicate timelines (legal will produce DocuSign within 24-48 hours). Attach exec_approval_form.pdf to the response. If SolaceMed accepts these conditions, execute the addendum and route to procurement.

Marissa Cole
VP, Global Sales — Redwood Inference
